correctness.rationale: Direct transfer of affine-on-dyadic-shell densities gives two bivariate generating functions; cancellation at two small kernel roots yields an explicit stationary two-time resolvent. Subtracting the stationary mean-square cancels its unit pole. For \(p>1/2\), remaining factors \(2t-1\), \(p-2qt\) and \(p-4qt\) are nonzero for \(|t|\leq1/4\), establishing exponential summability and justifying the infinite-time Green–Kubo formula. Symbolic simplification produces the exact rational \(\Gamma(p)\); derivative sign follows from an everywhere-positive cubic derivative, and the critical comparison follows from the vanishing instantaneous variance. Independent direct dyadic integration vs shell recurrence checked 24 rational finite-lag instances. No computation is used as proof of infinite convergence.

value.rationale: The originating literature singles out position correlations as transport-relevant and identifies the \(p=1/2\) infinite-density transition. This result exactly evaluates the natural Green–Kubo asymptotic variance, not an arbitrary finite lag or small parameter slice. It exhibits a sharp discontinuity of the long-time variance coefficient (4 versus 0 at the absorbing critical state), a strict entire-chaotic-range monotonicity law, and a divergent integrated correlation time despite collapse of single-step variance. The rational sum is not immediate from earlier \(O(n^2)\) finite-lag binomial expressions and carries a physically and mathematically interpretable noncommutation of limits.
